nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1}$, and let $s$ be an infinite sequence of states that visits every $F_j$ infinitely often, with counter sequence $c_0, c_1, \dots$. Then for every time $n$ and every $j$ with $c_n \le j \le k$ there is a time $m \ge n$ with $c_m = j$.
nodes.title: The degeneralization counter reaches every higher value

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1}$, let $s$ be an infinite sequence of states with counter sequence $c_0, c_1, \dots$, and let $i < k$ and $n$ satisfy $c_n = i$. If $m \ge n$ and $s_{j+1} \notin F_i$ for every $j$ with $n \le j < m$, then $c_m = i$.
nodes.title: The degeneralization counter waits for the awaited set

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton, $s$ an infinite sequence of states, and $c_0, c_1, \dots$ the counter sequence of $s$. For every $n$, $c_{n+1} = \mathrm{next}(c_n, s_{n+1})$, where $\mathrm{next}$ is the counter update of $g$.
nodes.title: Recursion step of the counter sequence

nodes.summary: For every generalized Büchi automaton $g$ and every infinite sequence of states $s$, the counter sequence of $s$ has value $0$ at time $0$.
nodes.title: The counter sequence starts at zero

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with $k$ acceptance sets and let $s = (s_0, s_1, \dots)$ be an infinite sequence of states. The counter sequence $c_0, c_1, \dots$ of $s$, with values in $\{0, \dots, k\}$, is defined by $c_0 = 0$ and $c_{n+1} = \mathrm{next}(c_n, s_{n+1})$, where $\mathrm{next}$ is the counter update of $g$. So $c_n$ is the counter after reading the states $s_1, \dots, s_n$; the state $s_0$…
nodes.title: Counter sequence of a state sequence

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1}$ and counter update $\mathrm{next}$, let $s$ be an infinite sequence of states, and let $c_0, c_1, \dots$ be any sequence in $\{0, \dots, k\}$ with $c_{n+1} = \mathrm{next}(c_n, s_{n+1})$ for every $n$. Let $a \le b$ be times with $c_a = 0$ and $c_b = d \le k$, and suppose $c_t \ne k$ for every $t$ with $a < t < b$. Then for every…
nodes.title: The degeneralization counter crosses every value below its target

nodes.summary: A generalized Büchi automaton with states $S$ and symbols $\Sigma$ is a nondeterministic automaton (a labelled transition relation on $S$ together with a set of start states) equipped with a natural number $k$ and $k$ acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1} \subseteq S$. A run is accepting when it visits every acceptance set infinitely often.
nodes.title: Generalized Büchi automaton

nodes.summary: A word is accepted by the degeneralized Büchi automaton iff it is accepted by the generalized Büchi automaton.
nodes.title: Degeneralization preserves the language

nodes.summary: An infinite word $x$ belongs to the language of a generalized Büchi automaton $g$ with acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1}$ iff there is a run $s$ of $g$ on $x$ such that for every $j < k$ there are infinitely many times $t$ with $s_t \in F_j$. Here a run of $g$ on $x$ is an infinite sequence of states $s_0, s_1, \dots$ with $s_0$ a start state and a transition from $s_i$ to $s_{i+1}$ labelled $x_i$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Language of a generalized Büchi automaton

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1}$ and counter update $\mathrm{next}$. If $i \in \{0, \dots, k\}$ satisfies $i < k$ and the state $t$ is not in $F_i$, then $\mathrm{next}(i, t) = i$.
nodes.title: The degeneralization counter stays when the awaited set is missed

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1}$, let $i \in \{0, \dots, k\}$ be a counter value and let $t$ be a state of $g$. If $i < k$ and $t \in F_i$, then the counter update of $i$ at $t$ is $i + 1$.
nodes.title: The degeneralization counter advances on a hit

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with $k$ acceptance sets and let $i \in \{0, \dots, k\}$ be a counter value. If $i = k$, then for every state $t$ of $g$ the counter update of $i$ at $t$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The degeneralization counter resets at the top

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1}$. The counter update takes a counter value $i \in \{0, \dots, k\}$ and a state $t$ of $g$ and returns a counter value in $\{0, \dots, k\}$: if $i < k$, it returns $i + 1$ when $t \in F_i$ and $i$ when $t \notin F_i$; if $i = k$, it returns $0$.
nodes.title: Counter update for degeneralization

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with $k$ acceptance sets. Its degeneralization is the Büchi automaton over the same alphabet whose states are the pairs $(s, i)$ of a state $s$ of $g$ and a counter value $i \in \{0, \dots, k\}$. can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
